entities.summary: Robert Dean Stockwell was an American actor, whose career in film and television spanned seven decades. As a child actor under contract to Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer, he appeared in Anchors Aweigh (1945), Song of the Thin Man (1947), The Green Years (1946), Gentleman's Agreement (1947), The Boy with Green Hair (1948), The Secret Garden (1949), and Kim (1950). As a young adult, he played a lead role in the 1957 Broadway play Compulsion and its 1959 film version; and in 1962 he played Edmund Tyrone in the film version of Long Day's Journey into Night, for which he won two Best Actor Awards at the Cannes Film Festival.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a child actor under contract to Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer, Dean Stockwell appeared in numerous films and television shows, including Anchors Aweigh (1945) and Gentleman's Agreement (1947). His performances helped establish him as a leading man in Hollywood during the 1940s and 1950s.
